articles.title: Brushed Steel Drift
articles.summary: Curling multi-directional brush; flowing highlight pools with perpendicular micro-scratches and satin sheen. A satin steel sheen with a gently mottled, worn look; the dashes blend into soft pools of light.
articles.what: Curling multi-directional brushed metal — flowing highlights, perpendicular micro-scratches, satin sheen pools. Up close: Soft pools of fine scratch dashes in mixed directions, tiny 6-12 px flecks angled at slightly different slants, clustered in patches inside the highlight. It looks like worn, hand-brushed steel; no hard shapes. From a distance: A satin steel sheen with a gently mottled, worn look; the dashes blend into soft pools of light. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Let Freedom Ring (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: fine.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Let Freedom Ring", or search for "Brushed Steel Drift".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof and doors on any base
Wide flats where the drift can flow
Numbers stay legible; flecks are tiny.
Visible: a speckled worn-steel grain in the highlight, a nice weathered satin
Pairs well with: matte, metallic, gloss, chrome.
pitfalls: Not Brushed Linear: strokes go several directions, not one clean line
Not a clean sandblast: the flecks are directional dashes
Avoid: swirl can fight clean stripes, keep off tight number decals.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.
